label: H.R. 9971
title: Advancing International and Foreign Language Education Act

items.snippet: These programs provide grants to institutions of higher education and related entities to (1) enhance instruction in international and foreign language studies, and (2) promote international business skills and education.

items.item: Graduate and Undergraduate Language and Area Centers
items.snippet: Specifically, it extends (1) the Graduate and Undergraduate Language and Area Centers and Programs, which include the National Resource Centers program;
Specifically, it extends (1) the Graduate and Undergraduate Language and Area Centers and Programs, which include the National Resource Centers program;

items.item: Undergraduate International Studies and Foreign Language Programs
items.snippet: (3) the Undergraduate International Studies and Foreign Language Programs;
and (4) the American Overseas Research Centers.
It also revises the program to permit graduate students to receive a stipend for the beginning, intermediate, or advanced study of a foreign language related to the student's area of specialization.

It also modifies the program, such as by (1) revising the types of available grants, and (2) allowing the Department of Education to establish a national database on international and foreign language education.
Specifically, it reauthorizes the Centers for International Business Education program.

lobbying.caption: From Senate lobbying disclosures (LD-2). A filing mentions this bill; it does not show what was asked for, which side the client took, or any contact with this member. Reported amounts cover the whole filing, not this bill alone.
lobbying.amount_note: Amounts are the income or expenses reported on the whole LD-2 filing, not money spent on this bill.

caption: This shows who the bill names and who lobbied on it. It does not show who gains or loses, and lobbying can be for or against a bill.

R000305.label: Overlap, not proof of influence.
R000305.caption: Money from this member's itemized individual donors (over $200) whose self-reported employer falls in an industry that also has a client lobbying on this bill. Correlation only; not a quid pro quo. Donors give to campaigns for many reasons, and a lobbying client may have opposed the bill.
R000305.note: None of the lobbying clients on this bill matched an industry rule, so there is nothing to compare.
